sources.title: Sand Deformation Mechanisms and Earth Pressures Mobilised with Retaining Wall Movements
Sand Deformation Mechanisms Mobilised with Active Retaining Wall Movement
Earth Pressures Mobilised in Dry Sand with Active Rigid Retaining Wall Movement
A new macro-element model encapsulating the dynamic moment-rotation behaviour of raft foundations
sources.review_scope: Text search for Hostun, triaxial and volume; this is a centrifuge/foundation-response paper, not an identified source for the four workbook triaxial histories.

scope: Six Deng-cited triax-CD-2 groups only; Heron-cited triax-CD-1 remains unresolved.

findings.locator: Deng thesis PDF p.107, printed p.81, Table 3.3
findings.finding: Thesis relative densities conflict with the six GEOLAB worksheet group labels. Do not select a density or derive a specimen void ratio until state timing and curve correspondence are resolved.

findings.locator: Deng thesis PDF p.108, printed p.82, Fig.3.20; companion PDF p.27, Fig.3
findings.finding: Both original figures explicitly label the abscissa Shear strain (%), while the curated/workbook channels are labelled Axial strain. The source does not establish a strain definition or valid conversion in the reviewed passages. Do not silently treat this as axial strain or apply a fixed factor.

findings.locator: Companion PDF p.7, Tables 2-3; thesis PDF p.107, Tables3.2-3.3
findings.finding: Material index limits and peak dilation angles are reported. Peak dilation angles are scalar derived summaries, not volumetric-strain histories. No recoverable volume-history plot was found in these reviewed triaxial figures.
New and used Hostun sand have distinct reported grain sizes. Generic Hostun labels do not prove shared material batch or preparation.

findings.locator: Deng thesis Sec6.2, PDF p.187 (printed p.161), Fig6.2 and Table6.2; page visually checked
findings.finding: A second presentation of the same six pressure/density groups again explicitly labels shear strain and reports half/full peak-deviator-stress mobilisation strains. This makes a one-off figure-label typo less plausible, but still does not define a conversion to axial strain. Table6.2 is a source-derived summary, not an independent dataset or a recovered volume history.
findings.use: Additional author-clarification locator only; no numerical curve matching, new fitting objective or strain conversion.

decisions.response_exposure: Published stress-strain figures and summary tables were read and visually inspected. No raw response rows, digitization, curve fitting or model comparison performed; do not claim unseen source curves.

remaining_questions: Which exact specimen and state stage correspond to each workbook Dr label and thesis table row?
Does Shear strain denote axial strain under a plotting error, maximum shear strain, or another defined measure?
Can original axial/radial or volumetric strain histories and apparatus/area corrections be recovered for the six CDC tests?
Recover Heron full-thesis preparation and specimen tables separately; do not borrow Deng states or index limits across batches.

heron_repository_followup.availability: Repository metadata states the thesis is not available until author agreement. Public ORIGINAL bundle returns zero bitstreams.
heron_repository_followup.request_route: University Library private-study/non-commercial research copy request; repository states copies must not be saved in shared facilities. No request made.
heron_repository_followup.open_companion_search: Downloaded public Heron/Haigh/Madabhushi foundation macro-element manuscript. Its text does not establish correspondence to the four GEOLAB triaxial curves; no missing triaxial volume channel recovered.
